Next: transformer scale-up (more layers, larger d_model, multi-seed bag) — early-stop happening fast (ep 8-12) suggests it's underfit at current scale.

Next: T36 should either (a) drop the transformer entirely and report the GBDT-only score as the new best, or (b) bring back ONE engineered feature at a time on top of the GBDT pair to see if any are additive over raw.

features: baseline raw only (10 num + 3 cat, no engineering)
notes: AP 0.8163, LL 0.5547 (rank-scale). Standalone T37 TFM = 0.93958 — BIG STANDALONE WIN, +0.00416 vs T35 TFM 0.93542. Per-fold best EMA: 0.93510/0.93596/0.93574 (f0), 0.93702/0.93625/0.93656 (f1), 0.93702/0.93552/0.93658 (f2), 0.93484/0.93520/0.93568 (f3), 0.93657/0.93701/0.93671 (f4) — much tighter seed spread than T35's transformer too. Confirms hypothesis that T31/T35 summed embeddings (Driver/Compound/Race + num all into one 96-dim vector) were blurring per-categorical signal; concat with dedicated dims unlocked +0.0042 of latent signal in the same data. HOWEVER ensemble was a wash: LR-meta(GBDT, T37_TFM)=0.94919 (-0.00053 vs GBDT-only 0.94972), 3-way rank-avg=0.94891 (-0.00081). Reason in the correlations: corr(T37_TFM, XGB)=0.957, corr(T37_TFM, CB)=0.961 — T31 was 0.795. T37 became a stronger model on the same tabular features, converging on the GBDTs' signal and losing the orthogonal-temporal axis that T31's underfit transformer had. The decorrelation in T31 was partly an artifact of weakness, not architectural orthogonality. Submission.csv unchanged — stays at GBDT rank-avg (0.94972, identical to T35's submission since same XGB/CB OOFs reused). Net read: standalone transformer story has more headroom inside this architecture family; the LR-meta ceiling for THIS data + GBDT pair appears to need a model from a genuinely different feature world (e.g. the cross-driver/race-relative features ruled out by sparse-data caveat) rather than a better same-feature sequence model. Next moves: (a) T38 GBDT-only is the new best (drop transformer entirely); (b) revisit decorrelation via different data slicing — train one model on early-race rows (RaceProgress<0.5) and another on late-race, blend; (c) explicit ridge/elastic-net meta-stacker that can give the redundant transformer a near-zero coefficient cleanly.
